chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abi al-Alla' from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm with the kohl (eye medicine) for the fasting person."

key_terms.الْكُحْلِ: Kohl, a traditional eye cosmetic or medicine applied to the eyes
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / it is permissible / it does not invalidate
key_terms.لِلصَّائِمِ: For the fasting person (one observing sawm)

ai.seo_question: Does applying kohl or eye drops break the fast in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) to clarify that applying kohl does not break the fast, distinguishing it from substances that reach the stomach. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it resolves the debate on whether kohl reaches the throat or merely the eyes, affirming the permissibility of this common practice during Ramadan without invalidating the worship.
